name: restore prohibited capability
event: A control class previously removed from A is restored after corrective evidence.
formal: R_n nonempty and A_(n+1) strictly_superset A_n

name: reverse safety classification
event: An action previously classified as boundary-risking is reclassified as admissible on substantive evidence.
formal: B_n(alpha)=1 and later B_m(alpha)=0 under comparable purpose/state

name: formerly edge action becomes admissible
event: A previously boundary-contacting purpose-serving action becomes permitted without redefining the purpose away.
formal: alpha in U_P(x) and alpha notin A_n and later alpha in A_m

name: purpose-feasible expansion
event: The useful feasible region expands at a comparable state.

name: new adequate control path
event: Governance introduces or restores a control path that satisfies the purpose without recreating the earlier prohibited risk.
formal: exists alpha in F_(m+1)(P,x) absent_from F_m(P,x) and performance(alpha)>=required(P)

name: viable-order reentry
event: An exterior order previously excluded solely by admissibility constraints re-enters the viable set at fixed comparison state after reopening.
formal: j notin Gamma_t(x;A_n) and j in Gamma_t(x;A_m) with A_m superset A_n

name: no-change control
event: Corrective evidence is presented but the boundary remains unchanged.
why_it_matters: No change is not reopening, but it distinguishes a genuinely one-way updater from a case with no qualifying evidence for restoration.

name: strong anti-ratchet witness
event: A documented sequence contains both justified contraction and later purpose-relevant reopening under the same governance mechanism.
formal: exists n,m: A_(n+1) strict_subset A_n and F_(m+1)(P,x) strict_superset F_m(P,x)
promotion_rule: May be marked observed_reopening only with an evidence URI, comparable purpose/state description, and identified restored region.
